feedback.details: shared/sprint-count.ts line 10 uses `/^##\s*Sprint\s+\d+/gim` with `^` anchor and `m` (multiline) flag. Only headings starting at column 1 are matched. Verified by running the function.

Tested the exact contract scenario: spec with '## Sprint 1' and '## Sprint 2' as line-start headings, plus 'builds on Sprint 3 features' in prose and '> ## Sprint 4' blockquoted — returns 2. Verified by execution.
Test in sprint-count.test.ts 'counts standard line-start headings' verifies a spec with four '## Sprint N' headings returns 4. Test passes.

conversation-logger.ts line 41-43 prepends fileTimestamp() to the base name, producing filenames like '2026.04.12-14.30.00-sprint-2-attempt-0-generator.md'. Tests verify TIMESTAMP_RE pattern /^\d{4}\.\d{2}\.\d{2}-\d{2}\.\d{2}\.\d{2}/. Verified by running createConversationLog.

Test 'resume does not overwrite prior logs' in conversation-logger.test.ts creates two logs for the same sprint/attempt with a 1.1s delay and verifies both files exist with different timestamps. The mechanism works because fileTimestamp() is called fresh each time. Minor risk: if two runs happen within the same second, filenames could collide (unlikely but possible).

harness-claude/contract.ts line 33 calls createConversationLog(workDir, 'contract-negotiation', sprintNumber). Test 'contract negotiation logs have timestamped names' verifies the filename matches TIMESTAMP_RE and contains 'sprint-3-contract-negotiation.md'.

All four agent types use createConversationLog: Generator (generator.ts:56), Evaluator (evaluator.ts:55), Planner (planner.ts:111), Documenter (documenter.ts:53), and contract-negotiation (contract.ts:33). All go through the same path that prepends fileTimestamp(). Tests verify Generator, Evaluator, Planner, Documenter, and contract-negotiation log types. No log file is written without a timestamp prefix.

fileTimestamp() in logger.ts uses getResolvedTimezone() which returns configuredTimezone (set by setDisplayTimezone). harness.ts line 35 calls setDisplayTimezone(config.tzDisplay). Verified by execution: setting timezone to 'America/New_York' produces timestamps 4 hours behind UTC, matching the configured timezone. Same timezone logic used for terminal output (timestamp() function).

FAIL: Span names and log filenames use INDEPENDENT fileTimestamp() calls at different times. In sprint-attempts.ts:37, the generator span is named with fileTimestamp() at time T1, but in harness-claude/generator.ts:56, createConversationLog calls fileTimestamp() at time T2 (potentially seconds later). The timestamps will differ, making cross-referencing unreliable. The timestampedName property is exposed on ConversationLogger but never used to set the span name. The span name and log filename are not guaranteed to match.
Grep for '@anthropic-ai', 'claude-agent-sdk', 'openai', '@google' in shared/ returns zero matches. The DI architecture boundary is maintained.

fileTimestamp() is defined once in shared/logger.ts (line 58) and imported everywhere: conversation-logger.ts, harness.ts, sprint-attempts.ts, sprint-success.ts. All log-writing and span-naming code paths call this single utility. DRY principle followed.

tests/sprint-count.test.ts has 10 tests covering: (1) standard headings counted (4 headings → 4), (2) inline prose references not counted ('builds on Sprint 3 features'), (3) blockquoted headings not counted ('> ## Sprint 3'), (4) indented headings not counted ('  ## Sprint 3'), (5) backtick-quoted references, (6) case-insensitive matching, (7) varied whitespace, (8) zero sprint headings, (9) complex acceptance criteria scenarios. All pass.

fileTimestamp() in logger.ts has try/catch: if timezone parsing fails (invalid en-GB format), falls back to formatIsoAsFileTimestamp(). If an invalid timezone throws, the catch block logs a debug warning and returns UTC-based timestamp. Verified by execution with 'Invalid/Zone' — falls back to UTC and logs warning. The function never crashes. Minor issue: the catch variable 'err' is unused (lint warning), but functionally correct.

overallSummary: Sprint 1 implements both features (regex fix and timestamp log filenames) with high quality. The sprint-counting regex correctly uses ^ anchor with multiline flag and has excellent test coverage (10 tests). Timestamp log filenames work correctly with timezone support and graceful fallback. However, the Langfuse span names alignment criterion fails: span names and log filenames use independent fileTimestamp() calls at different times, producing different timestamps that cannot be reliably cross-referenced. The timestampedName property is exposed but never used for span naming. This misalignment scores 5/10, below the 7/10 threshold.
